brief:
Human Rights Watch warned that an International Criminal Court pretrial chamber decision risks denying accountability for grave crimes in Afghanistan. On November 12, 2026, the chamber effectively closed the court's investigation into the situation, citing lack of activity. The closure halts scrutiny of alleged crimes by US forces, Afghan government troops, and other parties before the Taliban took power in August 2021.

The decision narrows pathways to justice for victims of serious violations committed during decades of conflict, the rights organization said. Human Rights Watch did not specify what activity the pretrial chamber deemed insufficient to justify keeping the investigation open.
dek: An International Criminal Court (ICC) decision risks hindering a path to justice for victims of grave crimes committed in Afghanistan, Human Rights Watch said today. On November 12, 2026, an ICC pretrial chamber, citing a lack of activity, effectively closed the court’s situation dealing with crimes by US, Afghan government, and other forces prior to the Taliban’s August 2021 takeover.
title: ICC closes Afghanistan inquiry, blocking justice for war crime victims
